examples.en: A die is a hexahedron with six faces.

examples.ko: 수학 시간에 육면체의 면과 모서리를 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: In math class we counted the faces and edges of a hexahedron.

examples.ko: 이 상자는 육면체 모양이라서 쌓기 쉬워요.
examples.en: This box is shaped like a hexahedron, so it's easy to stack.

examples.ko: 종이 한 장으로 육면체를 만드는 방법을 알아요?
examples.en: Do you know how to make a hexahedron from one sheet of paper?
The teacher drew a picture of a hexahedron on the board.

examples.ko: 주사위 같은 육면체에는 면이 여섯 개, 모서리가 열두 개 있어요.
examples.en: A hexahedron like a die has six faces and twelve edges.

explain: 수학 시간에는 '정육면체'(모든 면이 같은 정사각형)와 '직육면체'를 더 자주 말해요. '육면체'는 면이 여섯 개인 입체를 두루 가리키는 말이에요.

phrases.en: A die is shaped like a cube.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여섯 면이 모두 같은 정사각형인 육면체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A hexahedron whose six faces are all equal squares.

phrases.en: A milk carton is close to a rectangular box shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 면이 모두 직사각형인 육면체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A hexahedron whose faces are all rectangles.

phrases.example: 이 상자는 육면체 모양이라서 쌓기 쉬워요.
phrases.en: This box is a six-faced shape, so it's easy to stack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 모양을 설명할 때 '모양'과 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach '모양' when describing the shape of an object.

explain_en: In math class people more often say '정육면체' (a cube, with all faces equal squares) and '직육면체' (a rectangular box). '육면체' is the broader term for any solid with six faces.

examples.en: The organizing of citizens is moving along quickly.

examples.ko: 자료의 조직화가 잘 안 돼서 발표가 헷갈렸어요.
examples.en: The material wasn't well organized, so the presentation was confusing.
Organizing workers is not easy.
Volunteer activities need to be organized.

examples.ko: 조직화가 잘된 팀은 일을 빨리 끝내요.
examples.en: A well-organized team finishes work quickly.
I learned how to organize information in class.

explain: 사람이나 생각, 자료를 체계 있게 짜는 일을 말해요. 주로 글이나 뉴스, 수업에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '정리하다', '모으다'처럼 풀어서 말할 때가 많아요. '조직화가 필요하다·잘되다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: The workers became organized and made their voices heard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흩어져 있던 것이 체계 있게 짜이게 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that scattered people or things came to be organized into a system.

phrases.en: The presentation materials need to be organized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체계 있게 정리할 필요가 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something needs to be systematically arranged.

phrases.en: Many opinions came up during the organizing process.
phrases.nuance_ko: '과정'과 함께 쓰면 글이나 수업에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '과정', it sounds natural in writing or class.

explain_en: It refers to arranging people, ideas or materials in a systematic way. It is mostly used in writing, news and classes, and in everyday talk people often say things like '정리하다' or '모으다' instead. It goes with '필요하다' and '잘되다'.

en: to be proven; to be shown true

examples.en: That theory was proven by an experiment.

examples.ko: 그의 말이 거짓이 아니라는 것이 증명돼요.
examples.en: It is proven that his words are not false.
Skill is proven by results.
It is a medicine whose effect has not yet been proven.

examples.ko: 이 사진으로 제 말이 증명될 거예요.
examples.en: This photo will prove what I said.
It's a well-proven method, so you can trust it.

explain: '증명되다'는 어떤 사실이 근거나 결과로 확실해졌다는 뜻이고, 수학·과학·재판·뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 주어가 사람이면 '증명하다', 사실이나 이론이면 '증명되다'를 써요. 비슷한 '확인되다'는 있는지 없는지를 알게 된 것이고, '증명되다'는 옳다는 것을 보여 준 거예요.

phrases.en: That story hasn't been proven yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 근거가 부족해서 확실하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is not yet enough evidence to be certain.

phrases.en: The rumor was proven to be true.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~로 증명되다'로 결과가 확실해졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '~로 증명되다' pattern states that something turned out to be certain.

phrases.en: I want to prove my ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when a person is the subject.

explain_en: Shown true by logic or proof; general word. It means a fact has been made certain by evidence or results, common in math, science, trials and news. With a person doing it use 증명하다; with the fact or theory as subject use 증명되다. 확인되다 means you found out whether something is so, while 증명되다 means it was shown to be correct.

dis.h: shown true by logic or proof

p.n: 입증 stresses evidence; 증명 stresses proof.

en: the highest rank; the highest grade

examples.en: That student took the top spot in the class.

examples.ko: 최상위 성적을 받으려면 꾸준히 공부해야 해요.
examples.en: To get top-level grades, you have to study steadily.

examples.ko: 이 모델은 우리 회사 최상위 제품이에요.
examples.en: This model is our company's top-tier product.
I want to go to a top-ranked university.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 지난 시즌에 최상위로 올라갔어요.
examples.en: That team moved up to the top last season.
The top grade has separate benefits.

explain: '최상위'는 순위나 등급에서 맨 위를 말해요. '최상위권', '최상위 등급'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 경우가 많아요. 비슷한 '일등'은 한 명을 뜻하고, 최상위는 위쪽 무리를 넓게 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: That school is among the top schools in the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맨 위쪽 무리를 넓게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the whole top group, not just one.

phrases.en: This hotel received the highest grade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 등급 중 가장 높은 단계를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the highest level among grades.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 이번 시즌에 최상위에 올랐어요.
phrases.en: That team rose to the top this season.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순위가 맨 위로 올라갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a ranking climbs to the very top.

explain_en: Highest position in a ranking or group (최상위 성적) 최상위 means the very top of a ranking or grade. It often takes a following word, like 최상위권 and 최상위 등급. 일등 means exactly one winner, while 최상위 can also refer to the top group broadly.

en: to have a tough game; to fight hard

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 강한 상대를 만나 고전했어요.
examples.en: Our team struggled against a strong opponent.
It was my first time cooking that, so I struggled for a long while.

examples.ko: 신인 선수는 새 리그에서 고전하고 있어요.
examples.en: The rookie is having a hard time in the new league.

examples.ko: 시험 문제가 어려워서 학생들이 고전할 것 같아요.
examples.en: The exam questions are hard, so the students will probably struggle.
The shop that was struggling has gotten more customers lately.

examples.ko: 새 앱이 시장에서 고전하는 이유를 알아봤어요.
examples.en: I looked into why the new app is struggling in the market.

explain: '고전하다'는 강한 상대나 어려운 일 앞에서 힘들게 버틸 때 써요. 스포츠 기사에서 특히 자주 나와요. '고생하다'는 힘든 일을 겪는 것이고, '고전하다'는 경쟁에서 밀리면서 애쓰는 것이에요. 책 이름에 쓰는 '고전'과는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 초반에 고전했지만 끝까지 포기하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: Our team struggled early on but never gave up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기나 일의 처음 부분에서 힘들었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say it was hard at the start of a game or task.

phrases.en: We barely won after a hard struggle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 버틴 뒤에 결국 이겼을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for winning in the end after a hard fight.
phrases.en_equiv: to win after a tough fight

phrases.example: 우리 선수들이 강한 팀과 힘겹게 싸웠어요.
phrases.en: Our players fought hard against a strong team.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고전하다'보다 쉬운 말로, 같은 뜻을 일상 대화에서 풀어 쓸 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, everyday way to express the same idea.

explain_en: 고전하다 is used when you hold on with difficulty against a strong opponent or a hard task. It appears a lot in sports news. 고생하다 is going through hardship, while 고전하다 is straining while losing ground in a competition. It is a different word from 고전 meaning a classic book.

examples.en: This film won the grand prize at the film festival.
The grand prize goes to the best work.
Our school band won the grand prize.
Who is this year's grand prize winner?
I will practice hard aiming for the grand prize.
I watched the car racing grand prix on TV.

explain: '대상'과 거의 같은 뜻이지만, 대상은 학교 행사·방송·공모전에서 더 흔하고 그랑프리는 영화제·광고제·디자인 상처럼 외국 대회 이름을 따라 쓸 때 많이 들어요. 'F1 그랑프리'처럼 자동차 경주 대회 이름이기도 해요. '그랑프리를 받다', '그랑프리를 타다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: This work won the grand prize at the contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그랑프리와 거의 같고, 학교 행사나 방송에서 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same, and more common at school events and on TV.

phrases.en: That commercial won the grand prix at the advertising festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 받았다는 사실을 공식적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state formally that an award was won.

phrases.en: I watched an F1 Grand Prix race this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차 경주 대회 이름으로 쓰는 경우예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The use as the name of a car racing event.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '대상', but 대상 is more common for school events, TV shows and contests, while 그랑프리 is often heard for film festivals, ad festivals and design awards that follow foreign naming. It is also the name of car races, as in 'F1 그랑프리'. People say '그랑프리를 받다' or '그랑프리를 타다'.

examples.en: Our team won the final easily.
I thought we would win easily, but it was a close game.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 경선에서 낙승하리라고 다들 예상했어요.
examples.en: Everyone expected that candidate to win the primary easily.

examples.ko: 어제 경기는 우리가 낙승했지만 방심하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: We won yesterday's game easily, but we must not let our guard down.
We met a weaker team, so we won easily.

examples.ko: 낙승하려면 처음부터 점수 차를 벌려야 해요.
examples.en: To win easily, you need to build a score lead from the start.

explain: 스포츠나 선거 기사에서 많이 보이는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '쉽게 이기다'라고 하고, 아슬아슬하게 이길 때는 '신승하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 오늘 경기에서 낙승을 거뒀어요.
phrases.en: Our team won easily in today's game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기사에서 '이겼다'를 격식 있게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal, news-style way of saying someone won.

phrases.en: We beat the other team easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '낙승하다' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: What people usually say in daily conversation instead of 낙승하다.

phrases.example: 이번 선거는 그 후보가 낙승할 것 같아요.
phrases.en: That candidate looks likely to win this election easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 결과를 예상할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when predicting a future result.

explain_en: This word is common in sports and election articles. In daily talk people say '쉽게 이기다', and for a narrow win the word is '신승하다'.

examples.ko: 오늘 알바 대타 좀 구할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Could I find someone to cover my part-time shift today?
The manager sent in a pinch hitter at the last moment.
If you need a substitute, tell me anytime.

examples.ko: 이번 발표는 대타 없이 제가 직접 해야 해요.
examples.en: I have to do this presentation myself, with no substitute.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 대타로 나와서 안타를 쳤어요.
examples.en: That player came in as a pinch hitter and got a hit.

examples.ko: 갑자기 아픈 동료 대신 대타를 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I filled in for a coworker who suddenly got sick.

explain: 야구에서 온 말이지만 일상에서는 아르바이트나 모임에서 대신 일하는 사람을 가리켜요. '대타를 구하다', '대타를 뛰다'처럼 써요. 공식적인 자리에서는 '대리'나 '대신할 사람'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm looking for someone to cover my part-time shift today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대신 일할 사람을 찾을 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase when looking for a stand-in.

phrases.en: I worked as a stand-in for a sick coworker.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대타로'는 대신하는 역할을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '대타로' marks the role of standing in for someone.

phrases.en: I asked my friend to cover for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 대신해 달라고 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking someone else to take your place.

explain_en: It comes from baseball, but in daily life it means someone who covers for another person at a part-time job or an event. It is used as '대타를 구하다' (find a substitute) or '대타를 뛰다' (fill in). In formal settings people say '대리' or '대신할 사람'.

en: to be actively engaged; to act vigorously

examples.ko: 그 선수는 이번 시즌에도 맹활약하고 있어요.
examples.en: That player is performing brilliantly this season too.
The rookie actor shone in the drama.
He will play brilliantly in tomorrow's game too.
I feel proud seeing my junior doing so well.

examples.ko: 동생이 학교 대표로 나가 맹활약해서 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling represented the school, played brilliantly, and won a prize.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구들이 체육 대회에서 맹활약했으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope my classmates do brilliantly at the sports day.

explain: '맹활약하고 있다'처럼 지금 잘하고 있다고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '맹활약을 하다'라고 풀어서 말해도 돼요. 큰 경기나 큰 성공 뒤에 뉴스에서 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 오늘 경기에서 우리 선수가 맹활약을 했어요.
phrases.en: Our player performed brilliantly in today's game.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맹활약하다'를 풀어서 말한 모양이에요. 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spelled-out form of 맹활약하다 with the same meaning.

phrases.en: That actor was great in this movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맹활약하다'와 비슷한 뜻이에요. 크게 잘했다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 맹활약하다; praise for doing very well.

phrases.en: The player who did great last year is playing this year too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 잘한 사람을 말할 때 명사 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe someone who did well in the past.

explain_en: It is often used in the form '맹활약하고 있다' to say someone is doing great right now. You can also say it in the longer form '맹활약을 하다'. News articles use it often after a big game or a big success.

examples.en: The lineage of traditional crafts is in danger of dying out.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 삼 대째 명맥을 이어 오고 있어요.
examples.en: This shop has kept going for three generations.
The small theater troupe barely keeps itself alive.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 명맥도 겨우 이어 가는 처지예요.
examples.en: That school is barely holding on to its existence.

examples.ko: 이 마을 축제는 명맥이 끊겼다가 다시 살아났어요.
examples.en: This village festival died out and then came back to life.
Young craftsmen gathered to keep the tradition alive.

explain: 주로 전통, 기술, 단체처럼 오랫동안 이어져 온 것이 사라지지 않고 남아 있는 상태에 써요. '끊기다', '잇다', '유지하다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 일반적인 '목숨'이나 '존재'보다 '이어져 온 흐름'이라는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 오랫동안 명맥을 잇고 있어요.
phrases.en: That shop has kept its tradition alive for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전통이나 기술이 이어지게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means keeping a tradition or skill going.

phrases.en: This dance almost died out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이어져 온 것이 사라질 위기일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something handed down is about to disappear.

phrases.example: 작은 극단이 겨우 명맥을 유지하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The small theater troupe is barely surviving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렵지만 겨우 남아 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something barely holding on despite difficulty.

explain_en: It is mostly used for something long-lasting, like a tradition, skill or organization, that is still surviving. It often appears with '끊기다' (be cut off), '잇다' (continue) and '유지하다' (maintain). It feels like a continuing line rather than plain '목숨' (life) or '존재' (existence).

examples.ko: 우리 팀 투수가 오늘 무실점으로 경기를 끝냈어요.
examples.en: Our pitcher finished the game today without giving up a run.

examples.ko: 수비가 단단해서 세 경기 연속 무실점이에요.
examples.en: The defense is solid, so it's three games in a row without conceding.

examples.ko: 무실점 승리를 거둔 선수들이 환하게 웃었어요.
examples.en: The players who won with a shutout smiled brightly.

examples.ko: 무실점에 가까운 경기였는데 마지막에 한 골을 내줬어요.
examples.en: It was almost a clean sheet, but we gave up a goal at the end.
The defenders stayed focused to the end to keep the clean sheet.

examples.ko: 올해 목표는 무실점 경기를 열 번 하는 거예요.
examples.en: This year's goal is to have ten clean-sheet games.

explain: '실점'이 점수를 내주는 것이라면 '무실점'은 하나도 내주지 않은 경우예요. 축구에서는 '클린시트'라고도 해요. '무득점'은 반대로 점수를 못 낸 경우라서 헷갈리지 않게 조심해요.

phrases.example: 오늘 우리 팀이 무실점 경기를 했어요.
phrases.en: Our team played a shutout game today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수를 하나도 내주지 않은 경기를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a game in which no points were conceded.

phrases.en: The pitcher held the other team scoreless for six innings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 점수를 못 내게 막았다는 뜻으로 야구에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in baseball to say the opponent was kept from scoring.

phrases.example: 팀이 다섯 경기째 무실점 행진을 이어 가요.
phrases.en: The team is extending its streak of not conceding a point to a fifth game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수를 안 내주는 경기가 계속 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when games without conceding keep happening in a row.

explain_en: If '실점' is conceding points, '무실점' is conceding none at all. In football it is also called '클린시트'. '무득점' is the opposite case, scoring nothing, so don't mix them up.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 재미도 있고 문학성도 높아요.
examples.en: This novel is fun and also has high literary value.
That writer was recognized for literary quality.

examples.ko: 심사위원들은 작품의 문학성을 가장 중요하게 봤어요.
examples.en: The judges valued the literary quality of the work most.
People judge the literary value of web novels differently.
I want to write something with literary quality.

examples.ko: 문학성이 떨어진다고 해서 나쁜 책은 아니에요.
examples.en: A book with less literary value isn't necessarily a bad book.

explain: 작품이 문학으로서 예술적 가치가 있는지 말할 때 써요. 흔히 '재미'나 '대중성'과 나란히 놓고 비교해요. '문학적'은 분위기나 표현이 문학 같다는 느낌에도 쓰지만 '문학성'은 작품 평가에 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: This poetry collection is rated as having high literary value.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품의 예술적 가치가 크다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a work has great artistic value.

phrases.example: 이 소설은 재미는 있지만 문학성이 부족해요.
phrases.en: This novel is fun, but it lacks literary value.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재미와 비교해서 아쉬운 점을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to note a shortcoming compared with entertainment value.

phrases.example: 그 작품은 문학성을 인정받아 상을 탔어요.
phrases.en: That work won a prize for its recognized literary value.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평가를 받아 가치를 인정받았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a work's value is officially recognized.
phrases.en_equiv: to be recognized for literary value

explain_en: It is used when talking about whether a work has artistic value as literature, and is often compared with 'fun' or popular appeal. '문학적' can also describe a literary feel or style, but '문학성' appears more when evaluating a work.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 수비력이 약해서 점수를 많이 내줘요.
examples.en: Our team's defense is weak, so we give up a lot of points.

examples.ko: 이번 시즌에는 수비력도 눈에 띄게 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: This season our defense has noticeably improved too.
When it comes to defense, our team is the best in the league.
The offense is good, but the defense is lacking.
We train every day to build up our defense.

examples.ko: 수비력에서는 상대 팀이 한 수 위예요.
examples.en: In defense, the opposing team is a step above.

explain: '공격력'과 짝을 이루는 말로, 주로 스포츠에서 막는 힘을 말해요. 막는 행동 자체는 '수비'라고 하고, 그 능력을 말할 때 '수비력'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이 팀은 수비력이 강해서 잘 안 져요.
phrases.en: This team has strong defense, so it doesn't lose easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수비력'의 좋고 나쁨을 말할 때 '강하다', '약하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with 강하다 or 약하다 to describe how good a team's defense is.

phrases.en: The coach ran drills to build up our defense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력을 더 좋게 만들 때 '키우다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 키우다 when you improve or build up the ability.

phrases.example: 수비력이 좋은 팀이 우승할 때가 많아요.
phrases.en: Teams with good defense often win the championship.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수비력'을 꾸미는 말과 함께 팀이나 선수를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe a team or player by its defensive ability.

explain_en: It pairs with '공격력' (offensive power) and mostly refers to the ability to defend in sports. The act of defending is '수비', and '수비력' is the ability to do it.

examples.ko: 올해 야구 신인왕은 스무 살 투수예요.
examples.en: This year's baseball rookie of the year is a twenty-year-old pitcher.
That player won the rookie of the year title.
The candidates for rookie of the year were narrowed to three.
The pitcher won rookie of the year in his debut year.
After being chosen rookie of the year, interviews increased.

examples.ko: 골프 대회에서 신인왕에 오르는 게 목표예요.
examples.en: My goal is to win rookie of the year at the golf tour.

explain: 그해에 처음 데뷔한 선수 중 가장 뛰어난 사람에게 주는 상과 그 사람이에요. 야구나 골프 같은 스포츠에서 주로 쓰고, 가요나 연기 시상에서는 '신인상'이라고 해요. 야구와 골프 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: That pitcher is a rookie of the year candidate this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시즌 중에 뉴스에서 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Very common in news during the season.

phrases.en: That player was chosen as rookie of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수상 결과를 말할 때 써요. '차지하다'보다 투표로 정해진 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for award results; it suggests the winner was selected by vote.
phrases.en_equiv: to be chosen rookie of the year

phrases.en: That singer received the newcomer award.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가요나 연기 시상식에서는 '신인왕' 대신 '신인상'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: At music or acting awards, say '신인상' instead of '신인왕'.

explain_en: The award for the best newcomer of the year, and also the person who wins it. It is mostly used in sports such as baseball and golf, while for music or acting awards the word is 신인상. You often hear it in baseball and golf news.

examples.en: The ruling party won a landslide victory in this election.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 결승전에서 상대를 압승으로 꺾었어요.
examples.en: Our team beat the opponent by a landslide in the final.
A landslide was expected, but the result was a close call.

examples.ko: 이번 경기는 압승이라고 해도 될 만큼 점수 차가 컸어요.
examples.en: The score gap was big enough to call this game a rout.

examples.ko: 작년에 압승했던 선수가 올해는 예선에서 졌어요.
examples.en: The player who won by a landslide last year lost in the qualifiers this year.
Fans poured into the streets at the news of the sweeping victory.

explain: 선거나 경기에서 큰 차이로 이길 때 쓰고, '압승을 거두다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 비슷한 말로 '대승', '완승'이 있고, 반대는 '참패'예요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 첫 경기에서 압승을 거뒀어요.
phrases.en: Our team won the first game by a landslide.
phrases.nuance_ko: '압승'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말로, 큰 차이로 이겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase with 압승, meaning to win by a big margin.

phrases.en: That candidate won the election by a landslide.
phrases.nuance_ko: '압승을 거두다'를 짧게 동사로 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter verb form of 'to achieve a landslide victory'.

phrases.example: 우리 학교 농구부가 결승에서 대승을 거뒀어요.
phrases.en: Our school's basketball team won the final by a wide margin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '압승'과 비슷하게 크게 이겼다는 뜻이고, 경기에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 압승, meaning a big win, and used more often for games.

explain_en: Winning by overpowering the opponent; sports and elections. It is used when winning by a large margin in an election or game, and '압승을 거두다' is a common pairing. Similar words are '대승' and '완승', and the opposite is '참패'.
